reproduction_target: The computational half: Y-chromosome phylogenetic placement of 104 newly sequenced Cohanim plus 215 re-typed legacy samples, the pedigree-calibrated TMRCA estimates for the nine Cohen branches CB-01..CB-09 (Table 3), and the branch-qualification rule (>=5 members AND >=50% self-identified Cohanim). Wet-lab steps (recruitment, buccal-swab DNA extraction, Big Y-700 target-capture sequencing on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 / Complete Genomics DNBSEQ-T7) are scope-split out as OOS.
granularity_note: No workflow file (no Snakefile/CWL/Nextflow/WDL/Makefile) exists because no code repository is stated anywhere in the paper. Steps were therefore derived at one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation from the Methods sections 'Participants and sampling protocols', 'Genome Sequencing and variant calling', 'SNP-based phylogenetic dating', and 'Markers, Nomenclature, and Matching with Public Databases'. 11 steps total: 9 computational (|S|=9), 2 wet-lab (|W|=2). Several C-steps (C1-C3) are bundled inside the vendor 'Big Y-700 protocol' citation and could arguably be a single opaque step; they are kept separate because the prose names alignment, variant calling and STR genotyping as distinct products.

steps.label: Participant recruitment under Helsinki/IRB approval, informed consent, buccal-swab collection and genomic DNA extraction from 104 male Cohanim
Big Y-700 target-capture sequencing of 104 Y chromosomes at Gene by Gene on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 and Complete Genomics DNBSEQ-T7 (15 Mb NRY target, mean 35x, min 6x per site)
Read alignment of the 104 Y-chromosome captures to the GRCh38 reference, 'following the Big Y-700 protocol described in [8]' (Gene by Gene in-house pipeline)
Y-SNP variant calling on the aligned NRY reads per the Big Y-700 protocol (caller not named)
Y-STR genotyping producing 700+ marker values per sample (caller, panel definition and calling thresholds not named)

Backbone tree construction and MCMC TMRCA dating with BEAST v2.5.2 (strict clock, uniform prior on mutation rate, SNP rate 0.76e-9 subs/site/yr, locus-specific STR rates, coalescent constant-size tree prior, 100M generations sampled every 1,000, ESS>200 convergence check)
SNP branch-length to time conversion T = S / (mu x C) with union/intersect SNP coverage computed over the FTBED regions (11.25 Mb of NRY) 'as described by [13]'

STR-based branch-length estimation by modelling SNP-based TMRCA as a function of STR genetic distance with a GAM in the R package mgcv v1.8.28, applied to branches younger than 2,000 years (dual SNP/STR estimate)
Heterotachy correction via the relaxed-clock least-squares branch-length method of [15], with mutation-interval and mutation-rate uncertainty modelled as a gamma distribution
Cross-validation of phylogenies, alignment and branch ages against the YFull tree (https://www.yfull.com/tree/) and the ISOGG reference phylogeny

Matching of SNP haplotypes against the FamilyTreeDNA Discover tree / matching database (cited as the 'FamilyTreeDNA May 2025 Report', ~90,000 branches, >750,000 mutations) and assignment of CB-01..CB-09 under the qualification rule (>=5 branch members AND >=50% self-identified Cohanim; sensitivity discussed up to 75-80%)

gaps.where: whole paper (no Code Availability statement exists)
gaps.missing: No code repository of any kind is stated: no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo or Software Heritage link appears in the JATS full text or on the bioRxiv landing page. No BEAST XML, no GAM model script, no coverage/branch-length computation code, no branch-designation script is deposited or linked.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the BEAST XML(s), the mgcv GAM script, the FTBED coverage computation and the CB qualification script in a public repository with a release DOI (Zenodo), and add a Code Availability statement.

gaps.where: steps C1, C2, C3 (Genome Sequencing and variant calling)
gaps.missing: Alignment, variant calling and Y-STR genotyping are delegated wholesale to the proprietary commercial 'Big Y-700 protocol' operated by Gene by Gene (Houston, TX), cited only as reference [8]. The pipeline is not obtainable, not versioned and not described at the level of individual tool invocations.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the tool chain and parameter set actually used (aligner, caller, filters, versions), or provide called VCF/BAM-derived intermediates so the downstream analysis can be entered without re-running the vendor pipeline. Rubric ceiling: proprietary dependency caps these steps at NI.

gaps.missing: No per-sample identifiers and no sequence-data deposit. The 104 new Y sequences and the 215 re-typed legacy samples have no SRA/ENA/dbGaP/EGA/GEO accession anywhere in the paper. Samples are stated to be de-identified with only paternal geographic origin retained (Table 1), so no sample-to-data correspondence table exists. Verbatim Data Availability Statement: 'Sequencing results, including Y-STR profiles and initial phylogenetic placement on the FamilyTreeDNA (FTDNA) Discover tree, were uploaded to a dedicated project website ( https://www.familytreedna.com/groups/dnaprojects-2024/about ), which will become publicly accessible upon publication of this study.'
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit raw reads or NRY variant calls under a controlled-access accession (EGA/dbGaP) with a documented DAC path, plus a sample-to-accession mapping table. Note the deposit is promised conditionally ('upon publication'), so at assessment time the artifact is accidentally gated rather than legitimately controlled-access -> Data axis 1, not 2.

gaps.missing: Custom analysis assets are not public: the FTBED region definition used for union/intersect SNP coverage (11.25 Mb of NRY), the Mean Path Length (MPL) construction code, the relaxed-clock least-squares implementation of [15], and the branch-qualification/threshold-sensitivity script.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the FTBED interval file with a version, and the scripts implementing MPL, the relaxed clock and the CB thresholds.

gaps.where: steps C2, C3, C5, C7, C8
gaps.missing: 2a 版記載なし - the variant caller, the STR caller, the FTBED region file, the relaxed-clock implementation and the ISOGG nomenclature release carry no version identifier at all. Only two software versions are pinned anywhere in the paper: BEAST v2.5.2 (C4) and mgcv v1.8.28 (C6); the R interpreter version, CRAN snapshot/channel and platform are not stated, so there is no environment closure.
gaps.how_to_close: State every tool with an exact version, and ship a renv.lock / conda-lock / container digest covering the interpreter, package source and declared platform.

gaps.missing: Out-of-band, unpinned third-party reference resources. The FamilyTreeDNA Discover tree is a rolling commercial consumer database cited only by a report date ('FamilyTreeDNA May 2025 Report'); the YFull tree is cited by bare URL (https://www.yfull.com/tree/) with no version or snapshot date; ISOGG nomenclature has no release identifier. Both trees are continuously updated, so the branch topology and membership counts underlying CB-01..CB-09 are not addressable at a fixed state.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite a dated/DOI-versioned snapshot of each tree, or archive the exact subtree extracts used (node lists, member counts) as supplementary data. At Stage 2 these would be candidates for env_capture_class C (mutable-fetch-fatal) if consumed by code.

gaps.missing: No random seed is reported for the 100-million-generation MCMC run. Convergence is asserted via ESS>200 but the chain is not reproducible bit-for-bit; agreement can only be assessed distributionally against the reported TMRCA point estimates and 95% CIs (e.g. CB-01 TMRCA 833 BCE, CI 1289-440 BCE).
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed and ship the BEAST XML; otherwise the step is capped at RI with subflag distributional-only, which is where it already sits.

gaps.missing: Non-computational wet-lab work excluded from |S|: informed-consent recruitment of 104 Cohanim under National Helsinki Committee / Rambam Medical Center IRB approval, buccal-swab collection, genomic DNA extraction, and Big Y-700 target-capture sequencing on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 and Complete Genomics DNBSEQ-T7.
gaps.how_to_close: Out of scope for NASEM-2019 computational reproducibility; documentation audit only.
